To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the most effective reward system for knowledge sharing is one that is contingent on knowledge sharing behavior, that rewards are most appropriate for knowledge sharing within teams, that team based rewards are the most appropriate for knowledge within teams, and that company wide incentives are the most appropriate reward system for knowledge across work units.

monetary incentives can be used effectively to encourage knowledge sharing in organizations, and the most effective monetary rewards are those that are directly contingent on knowledge sharing, those based on team performance, and company wide incentives.
monetary rewards are an important factor in knowledge sharing, but their impact is mediated by the type of knowledge sharing behavior.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of monetary incentives in knowledge sharing in organizations and how they can be effectively used in the context of different knowledge sharing mechanisms.
how monetary rewards can be used effectively to foster knowledge sharing within and between work units.
the role of organizational reward systems in encouraging knowledge sharing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the role of monetary and non-monetary incentives in knowledge sharing depends on the mechanism of knowledge sharing and the type of knowledge sharing.
the role of rewards in encouraging knowledge transfer and sharing is contingent on the nature of the knowledge transfer and sharing mechanism.
the most appropriate rewards to encourage knowledge sharing in organizations are contingent on knowledge sharing behavior and are based on collective performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
monetary rewards have the greatest potential for encouraging knowledge sharing in organizational databases and formal interactions within or among teams.
monetary rewards are an important factor in fostering knowledge sharing, but their impact varies depending on the mechanism of knowledge sharing.
knowledge sharing is a complex process that is influenced by multiple factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
knowledge sharing is a complex social and organizational phenomenon, and that the role of rewards in fostering knowledge sharing is not straightforward.
monetary rewards have a role to play in knowledge sharing, but they are not the only way to encourage knowledge sharing.
the design and implementation of reward systems in organizations must be sensitive to the nature of knowledge sharing mechanisms and the role of knowledge sharing in the organizational context.
